newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Fresh supplies seen dampening prices.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Fresh supplies seen dampening prices.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to slide this week as two more ships have started to load fresh supplies of the commodity from the Philippines, vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"Buyers in the U.S. and Rotterdam can now heave a sigh of relief with more coconut oil loadings in the Philippines," said a senior trader.
MV Blue Sapphire started loading 35,000 tonnes of coconut oil yesterday after arriving in the southern Mindanao island on Monday.
Another vessel, MV Sun Sapphire, was also expected to have arrived in the Philippines to load another 25,000 tonnes of coconut oil.
Trading was quiet with most prices unchanged last week as supply fears eased with the loading of 35,000 tonnes of coconut oil in Europe-bound MV Luctor.
"Luctor is still in the country but it is expected to leave port shortly," said one trader.
Coconut oil supplies in Rotterdam dropped to 11,948 tonnes on June 2 from the previous 15,972.
Traders said domestic coconut oil and copra prices were also unchanged due to stable supplies.
Coconut oil in Manila was quoted at 16.70 pesos per kg on Monday while copra was pegged at at 10.50 pesos per kg.
